findings.evidence: PMCADemo/CameraActivity.java: onShutterKeyDown() calls camera.getNormalCamera().takePicture(null, null, null) -- conventional android.hardware.Camera capture, NOT CameraSequence.getPreviewSequenceFrames(). onFocusKeyDown()/onFocusKeyUp() call autoFocus()/cancelAutoFocus(). No code-level link found between CameraSequence/ScalarDaemon and ObjCamera/ObjEffect/PbCap (architecture E's object family); a shared-backend relationship with architecture B/F (SFRA/DMM, also served by ScalarDaemon) is more plausible but unverified (same daemon class family, no traced call graph).
findings.notes: EXPLICIT: does not declare that electronic capture via S2 works. CameraSequence is real and verified; its connection to the physical shutter button is unverified and would require new application-level integration work.

message_for_principal_claude.topic: Android-side physical shutter event delivery vs native LIRO/RelMgr
message_for_principal_claude.finding: On the Android side, the physical shutter key event reaches the app as a high-level Android framework callback (onShutterKeyDown/onFocusKeyDown in BaseActivity, based on standard Android KeyEvent dispatch), verified by direct reading of real PMCADemo source code. This is a separate, independently-documented software path from the native LIRO RelMgr queue (0x40193, handler 0x4379d838) that the main investigation tracks for S1/S2 bit masks. No evidence was found this session connecting the two paths (shared hardware interrupt dispatched twice vs. RelMgr bypassed for Android apps) -- flagged as an open question for the LIRO/RelMgr branch.
message_for_principal_claude.classification: VERIFICADO (Android-side callback existence and conventional takePicture wiring); NO VERIFICADO (relationship to native RelMgr queue)
